note: MasonryZap parameters in human units only: percents and plain addresses. No bps, no wei — deploy code converts (0.5 percent becomes 50 in the contract's routeFeeBps).

zap._feeRecipient: Wallet that receives the route fee — the DAO/Treasury wallet the other protocol fees route to (fees are always wallets in this protocol, never the Treasury contract). Set with setFeeRecipient after deployment.
zap._routeFeePercent: The one house toll (spec section 15): percent of the input taken once, before conversion, to the fee recipient — charged in the input asset on every route including swap(). 0.5 = one half of one percent. Worked example: zapping 1,000 USDC into a farm pool pays exactly 5 USDC of route fee and works the remaining 995 into the position. The Genesis LP route is EXEMPT — it always pays 0 here, because staking those shares into Genesis pool 1 charges the 0.5% Genesis LP deposit burn fee instead; one action never pays the toll twice. The Genesis standard route DOES pay it: pool 0 deposits are credited gross (no deposit fee exists there), so there is nothing to double. On-chain safety bound: the contract rejects any setting above 5 percent.
zap._routes: zap(inputToken, amountIn, destination, minOutput, deadline) is the generic entry; named wrappers: zapToGenesisLP, zapToFarmLevel, zapToFarmShare, zapToMasonry, zapToGenesisStandard, zapAssetToGenesisStandard. Every staking route ends STAKED for the caller (LP created and staked, or the share/standard token staked in the Boardroom / Genesis pool 0). swap(inputToken, amountIn, outputToken, minOut, deadline) is the engine's token-to-token route — the surface the frontend Swap page consumes (stable<->asset on each hooked pool, asset<->asset bridged through the stable). Accepted zap inputs: the stable for every route, plus each destination's own stake asset directly (vault shares into the LP routes, the standard asset into Genesis pool 0, xSHARE into the Masonry).
zap._wiring: Deploy order: staking stack first (MasonryGenesisStaking, ShareRewardPool with pid 0 = Level vault and pid 1 = Square vault, Boardroom initialized with the Square token as its share), then the zap against them. AFTER deploying the zap, wire it as the beneficiary-staking operator on all three surfaces or every zap-and-stake reverts: MasonryGenesisStaking.setZapOperator(zap) by the Genesis schedule's scheduler, ShareRewardPool.setZapOperator(zap) by the farm operator, Boardroom.setZapOperator(zap) by the Boardroom operator. The Genesis standard pool's stake asset is read from the staking contract at deploy time (its constructor forbids the reward token there) — the zap supports the stable, xTOMB or xSHARE as that asset and reverts at construction for anything it cannot price.
